text: Every codebase has an architecture diagram. And almost every one of them is lying.
speaker: am_michael

text: You draw the boxes on day one. The interface talks to features, features talk to services, and nothing reaches back up.
speaker: am_michael

text: Then someone ships on a Friday. One quiet import skips a layer. Nobody notices, and the diagram keeps smiling.
speaker: am_michael

text: Laymos moves that diagram out of your head and into one config file. Layers own folders. Modules draw borders inside them. Rules say who may depend on whom.
speaker: am_michael

text: Then it reads your real imports and compares. The moment code crosses a line that the config never allowed, lint fails and points at the exact file.
speaker: am_michael

text: So the architecture you drew is the architecture you have. Reviews argue about design, not about stray imports.
speaker: am_michael

text: Declare the layers. Let laymos check every import. Keep the diagram honest.
speaker: am_michael
